reason: The developmental environment provides signals for the stem-cell population to follow the fibroblast route described in the goal.
expectation: The signals will begin directing some of the cells toward a connective-tissue-producing fate.

effect: The signals directed a subset of cells toward fibroblasts and activated a collagen gene, producing messenger RNA for the next stage.
reaction: The connection between the external signal and selective gene activity is useful.
reason: The collagen messenger RNA is heading to ribosomes, where amino acids can be assembled into protein.

choice.combine: Developing fibroblasts with collagen messenger RNA

expectation: The fibroblasts will use the amino acids to make collagen precursor protein.

effect: The fibroblasts have translated collagen mRNA into procollagen, which is now in the ER and Golgi; the next goal is to build extracellular material.
reaction: The RNA-to-protein connection is clear, though the result repeats the picture description.
reason: The secretory vesicles are shown carrying procollagen from the Golgi and fusing with the membrane.
expectation: The vesicles will release procollagen outside the fibroblasts for further processing.

effect: The fibroblasts have released procollagen outside the cells, where it can be processed into collagen.
reaction: The sequence from gene activity to material outside the cell is clear.
reason: The collagen-processing enzymes are shown clipping secreted procollagen and linking the resulting collagen molecules.
expectation: The enzymes will process the procollagen and help form cross-linked collagen.

effect: The procollagen has become cross-linked collagen fibers that resist tension; the hydrated proteoglycans remain available to complete the extracellular material.
reaction: The tension arrows make the fibers' structural role clear.
reason: The proteoglycan description shows a water-rich gel with spaces for collagen fibers, suggesting they form the extracellular material together.
expectation: The fibers and hydrated gel will form a connective-tissue extracellular matrix.

effect: The collagen fibers and hydrated proteoglycans formed an extracellular matrix, with fibroblasts shown separately from it; the chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The cell-versus-matrix distinction is useful and clearly shown in the illustration plan.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the signal from a developing cell to collagen production and secretion connected gene activity to a tangible structural role.

leastWorthwhile.text: Some wonder text repeated the illustration descriptions rather than adding an explanation. Terms such as mesoderm and proteoglycan also appeared without much explanation.

surprise.text: The final illustration plan explicitly kept fibroblasts adjacent to the matrix rather than depicting the cells as becoming the material between them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the item descriptions supplied a plausible purpose for each combination.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because the sequence connected familiar gene expression to how tissue material is built, though I would welcome clearer explanations of specialist terms.
